intent:
Docs land in the SeaweedFS bucket `ov-sync`, laid out as
`<owner>/<repo>/{docs,.okf}/...` plus `<owner>/<repo>/_state/manifest.json`,
which CI writes and the consumer ignores. This ticket builds everything from
the bucket to OpenViking. CI uploads are `ci-openviking-sync`, which will
depend on this ticket. The design is section 3b of
`.okf/handoffs/bifrost-decision-models-ci-lab-auth-and-openviking-doc-sync-design.md`.

**The Go app** is a module in `new:applications/ov-sync-consumer/go.mod`. It
lives under the top-level `applications/`, beside `applications/migrations/`,
and not inside the Terraform root, so it can later move to its own repo the
way `JasperHG90/leo-webhook-exporter` did. It has two parts in one binary:

- An HTTP endpoint for the filer's `[notification.webhook]`. It checks the
  bearer token and publishes each event into a JetStream stream on NATS at
  `192.168.2.50:4222` (`docs/reference/nats.md`), with a `Msg-Id` for dedupe.
- A consumer that treats each event as "look at this file now", because the
  webhook delivers out of order. It reads the object's current state from the
  bucket and then writes the file to OpenViking or deletes it there. It maps
  `<owner>/<repo>/...` to `viking://user/jasper/resources/projects/<repo>/...`
  from its config. It runs a fixed worker pool behind a rate limit, acks only
  after OpenViking accepts, retries with backoff, and moves a message to a
  dead-letter subject after N tries. A periodic catch-up pass compares the
  bucket with OpenViking and repairs events that were lost.

Bucket access is keyless through minio-go web identity, as tempo does
(`docs/how-to/give-a-job-keyless-seaweedfs-access.md`). The OpenViking
credential is a Vault identity token, minted the way hermes and leo-consumer
mint theirs.

**Build and gates.** `new:applications/ov-sync-consumer/Dockerfile` builds a
static arm64 binary. `new:applications/ov-sync-consumer/justfile` has
`build`/`push`/`release` recipes that read the tag from the one
`ov_sync_consumer_image` line in `deployments/applications/services.tf` and
push to ghcr, as `deployments/applications/services/driftwatch/justfile`
does. `go vet` and `go test` join `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as local hooks
scoped to `^applications/ov-sync-consumer/`, so `just pre_commit` runs them.
The devcontainer has no Go toolchain today, so risk 3 decides how those hooks
get one.

**Wiring, per `.claude/rules/terraform-file-layout.md`:**

- `deployments/applications/storage.tf`: bucket `ov-sync` in `local.buckets`,
  with no static users. CI keys belong to `ci-openviking-sync`.
- `deployments/infrastructure/services.tf`: `ov-sync-consumer = "ov-sync"`
  in `local.seaweedfs_keyless_jobs`, and the webhook endpoint passed into
  `deployments/infrastructure/services/seaweedfs.hcl`. That job gains a
  `notification.toml` template with `path_prefixes = ["/buckets/ov-sync/"]`
  and the bearer token, on the standard `chrislusf/seaweedfs:4.48` image.
- `deployments/infrastructure/secrets.tf`: one random bearer token, written to
  KV under both the seaweedfs job's path and the consumer's path, because the
  `nomad-workloads` policy scopes each job to its own path.
- `deployments/infrastructure/variables.tf`: an `ov-sync-consumer` entry
  (`lab`/`jasper`) in `var.vault_openviking_workloads`. `deployments/infrastructure/oidc.tf`
  and `deployments/infrastructure/machine_roles.tf` already loop over that
  variable, so they need no edit.
- `new:deployments/applications/services/ov-sync-consumer.hcl` and its
  `nomad_job` in `deployments/applications/services.tf`. It runs on radxa
  beside NATS and OpenViking (`.okf/nodes/placement.md`), on a static webhook
  port that the `firewall_rules` there open to orangepi4a (192.168.2.29)
  only. The filer binds to loopback inside its container, but the webhook is
  an outbound call from there to `192.168.2.50:<port>`.
- Knowledge: a decision record for the bucket-to-queue-to-consumer design and
  its rejected `gocdk_pub_sub` backend. An `.okf/components/` page for the
  service. Updates to `.okf/nodes/placement.md` and `docs/reference/nats.md`
  for the new job and stream.

**Outcome:** with the job running, `mc cp` of a `.md` file to
`ov-sync/JasperHG90/localstack/docs/` can be read at
`viking://user/jasper/resources/projects/localstack/docs/` within 60 s, and
`mc rm` removes it within 60 s. This holds when OpenViking is stopped during
the copy and started again five minutes later. A burst of 200 files never
has more OpenViking requests in flight than the configured pool size.

## Could invalidate this plan

- **OpenViking may refuse the writes and deletes the consumer needs, made
  with a Vault identity token as a USER.** A lab/jasper USER token can create
  and replace a file through `content/write` (spike:ov-save-skill/2) and can
  mkdir, write and read on a fresh instance (spike:ov-fresh-instance/3).
  Untested: a write to a file under folders that do not exist yet, and a
  delete of a file and of a folder it leaves empty. Waiting on a spike.
- **The filer webhook may not behave in this job's shape.** The handoff's
  local spike showed the standard 4.48 image post filtered, bearer-authed
  JSON events for `ov-sync` writes, but its files are gone. It also never
  ran under `weed server -s3` with loopback binds, or from orangepi4a's
  podman bridge to a listener on radxa. If the webhook does not fire or
  cannot reach radxa, the event path has to change. Waiting on a spike.
- **The Go gates may need a toolchain the devcontainer lacks.** The repo has
  no Go and the devcontainer has no `go` binary. If prek cannot fetch a
  toolchain for a `language: golang` hook, in this container and in a fresh
  `.loop/worktrees/` checkout, the gate needs a devcontainer rebuild first
  or a containerized hook. Either changes how this ticket can pass its own
  gate. Waiting on a spike.
